RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the March 13, 2007/Phalguna 22, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Culture; Finance; Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas;
Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 155
344
New airport in Pune
1487. DR. ABHISHEK MANU
SINGHVI: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the present airport in Pune
is located in and shares its airstrips with
the Airforce-station due to which the airlines
and passengers face acute problems on
account of this;
(b) whether there is any plan to build a
new airport in Pune; and
(c) if so, whether a site has been
identified and by when the construction
will start?
Entry of private companies in ground
handling operation
†1488. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL:
SHRI MAHENDRA SAHNI:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to include private companies in crucial jobs
like ground handling;
(b) whether it is a fact that inclusion of
the said companies will see a 70 per cent
reduction in earnings of public sector
airlines;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) if not, Government's approach in
this regard;
(e) whether Government are
reconsidering the decision of merger of both
the public sector airlines; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Development of unprofitable airports
1489. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL:
Will the Minister of CIVIL  AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Airports Authority of
India (AAI) is contemplating to develop
some of the unprofitable airports in the
country;
(b) if so, the details of these airports;
and

Expenditure on staff welfare
1490. SHRI PRASANTA
CHATTERJEE:
 SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state the actual expenditure
incuned by Indian on account of staff welfare
during the last five years, year-wise and
head of account-wise?
Requirement of proficiency in English
for foreign pilots
1491. SHRI SHANT ARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the number of foreign pilots flying
passenger aeroplanes in India;
(b) whether these pilots are able to
speak and write in the English language;
and
(c) whether it is mandatory for the
candidates applying for flying passenger
aeroplanes that they should be able to speak
and write in the English language?
New equity norms for airlines
1492. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether, to ensure that the aviation
sector attracts only serious players in the
long run, Government have decided to raise
the bar and increase the minimum equity
needed to float an airline to Rs. 50 crore for
the first five aircrafts of an airline with large
aircraft fleet and to Rs. 20 crore for those
with smaller aircrafts;
(b) whether the Ministry issued a
notification with these changes that will
also apply to existing airlines which will be
given a year's time to bring their equity at
par with the rules; and
(c) if so, to what extent these changes
have been implemented?
Airports operational in HP
1493. SHRI SURESH BHARDWAJ:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the total number of airports in the
State of Himachal Pradesh which are
operational;
(b) whether Indian operates flights to
all these airports;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Fate of HAL airport
1494. DR. VIJAY MALLYA: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) what the fate of the HAL airport
will be once the international airport at
Bangalore becomes operational from 2008;
(b) whether the HAL airport will be
used commercially or returned to HAL; and
(c) by when Government propose to
take a decision on this as lack of decision
gives rise to wild rumours which affect the
real estate market?
International airport at Kannur, Kerala
1495. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) the present stage of the processing

346
and finalization of the decision about
building a new international airport at
Kannur, Kerala;
(b) the reasons for the delay in finalizing
a decision on this; and
(c) by when the final decision is likely
to be taken?
Development of airstrips by private
parties
1496. SHRI P.R. RAJAN: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) the number of airports for which
Government are allowing private players
to develop airstrips;
(b) the conditions laid out for these
private parties to set up airstrips in
airports; and
(c) whether Government will allow
private parties to develop their own
airports?
Bird-hit incidents at Delhi Airports
